fieldMarks: Typical skink with smooth, glossy overlapping scales, a cone-shaped head, cylindrical body and relatively small limbs; maximum snout-vent length 149 mm (Mesa, Arizona animals 68-118 mm, 160-230 mm total).

Usually light-centred dark spots (ocelli) on a light brown, bronze, yellowish-green or grey background; ocelli may merge into dark bands, some animals have dark lateral stripes and others lack ocelli.
Belly usually white; juveniles have a greenish tail.
behavior: Basks on open ground and uses dense vegetation, rocks or woody debris for cover.
Live-bearing (eggs retained until hatching); one or two litters of 2-20 in summer; mating likely in spring.
Eats insects, arachnids and small lizards, including its own young.
habitat: In Arizona found in and around potted plants, block walls, planters and shrubbery and inside garages and storerooms; in the native range it occupies open forest, Mediterranean and coastal scrub, palm oases, farms and gardens.
range: Native from Italy across the Mediterranean and Middle East to Pakistan and North Africa; introduced and established in Mesa, Arizona (first confirmed 2007) and reported established in Florida, Britain and France. NatureServe lists only Arizona as exotic for the US.
